newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Motor sees no big rise in Japan car exports.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Motor sees no big rise in Japan car exports.

text.p: Japan's automobile exports will not increase substantially despite a recent rise in Japan's overall trade surplus, Nissan Motor Co Ltd president Yoshikazu Hanawa told reporters on Monday.
"Exports from the car industry will not be a major factor in the trade surplus because the car industry has been developing overseas production and increasing procurement from overseas," Hanawa said.
Japanese Finance Ministry data released on Monday showed that Japan's trade surplus more than doubled in April to 831.48 billion yen.

Hanawa also said he was not surprised by the recent sharp appreciation of the yen, which followed a long-term rally in the dollar that peaked early this month around 127 yen, the greenback's highest level in more than four-and-a-half years.
Noting that Nissan Motor has had to deal with exchange rates of 90 yen and less to the dollar in the past, Hanawa said that fluctuations of five yen or so were a routine matter.
He also said that the recently passed liberalisation of Japan's foreign exchange law will help the company cut costs in its overseas transactions.

Hanawa was speaking at a news conference to unveil Nissan's new Caravan/Homy Elgrand minivan. The company aims to sell 5,000 of the minivans a month, although Hanawa said Nissan has no plans to export them.
